## Design

### 2026-10-12 – Devlog 01: first layout

**2h**

Devlog 01: first layout

started the pcb vise for CAD week. i want to hold a board while soldering and flip it over without taking it out

made the first layout in FreeCAD: a base, two uprights, and a frame with jaws that slide on steel rods. aiming for boards 30-160 mm wide. the main sizes are editable so i can adjust it as i go

looked at my ESC to work out how to hold it. there's too much stuff near the right edge for a normal grip, so i'm using its four mounting holes. i'll make separate grips for other boards

checked the frame at several angles and tried a few board sizes. nothing hit in this first layout, but it only has an empty board shape so far. still need to check the components and connectors

also made a small rod-hole and M6 nut-pocket sample for build week. i'll use that to choose the fit before printing the full parts

next are the jaw locks, pivot bolts and connections between the base pieces. nothing printed yet

### 2026-10-14 – Devlog 02: clamps, pivots and base

**4h**

Devlog 02: clamps, pivots and base

added the jaw locks. each jaw has a slit and an M4 screw that tightens it around the front rod with an Allen key

the ESC adapters now screw onto the jaws. also made TPU grips with slots for ordinary board edges. they use the same holes, so i can swap them without replacing the jaws

worked on the pivots too. M6 bolt heads sit in pockets in the carriers, and the knobs hold the nuts. TPU rings go between the frame and uprights to help hold the angle. i'll have to test how well that works when it's printed

the base pieces now bolt together. added lids for the weight pockets and TPU covers for the feet. found that the outer lid-screw tips hit the covers, so made recesses inside to clear them

checked for parts hitting each other as the frame turns and tried the jaws at different widths. also adjusted the print orientations and made a second fit sample for the smaller nuts

exported the STLs and STEP file, then updated the hardware list and assembly notes. nothing printed yet. the populated ESC clearance, base weight and remaining fits still need work before build week

### 2026-10-15 – Devlog 03: board clearance and ballast

**2h**

Devlog 03: board clearance and ballast

checked the holder with the ESC components in place. some models were missing, including the XT60, so i left extra room around those parts

the power connector was too close to the fixed end of the holder. turned the ESC around so it faces the open space along the rods, and raised the adapters by 10 mm. the board screws are now M3 x 25

checked room for the connectors and a screwdriver, then checked clearance as the frame turns. the cable bends still need confirming. the normal edge grips stay at the original height

the old weight pockets were too small. made the feet longer and the pockets deeper, with TPU liners for four steel blocks. the blocks should weigh about 1.36 kg together

worked through the tipping calculation using just the steel blocks and rods. it gives a margin just over 1.5 for a 5 N sideways force at 225 mm above a flat bench. that still needs a real test, and it doesn't tell me whether the feet will slide

updated the lids and screws, added the drawings and changed the hardware list. next are prices, the remaining fits and a slicer review. printing comes during build week

### 2026-10-15 – Devlog 04: hardware and print setup

**3h**

Devlog 04: hardware and print setup

went through the hardware list and found actual parts for it. the standard M3 washers are a little wider than the ones i had modelled, and the M4 washers are thinner. changed those and checked the ESC again. the larger washers still clear the available component models

checked the screw lengths and nut pockets too. found cheaper rods at $5.79 each, and put all the screws, nuts and washers in one cart. that order is $8.74 before shipping. the full parts list is $39.92 before shipping, tax and cutting the steel

set up the print plates for my P1S and 0.4 mm hardened nozzle. the first slice caught two problems: the right-hand base bars had ledges hanging in the air, and the feet had unsupported roofs over the bar slots. flipped the right bars and added supports in the feet

the revised plates slice without warnings. saved six Bambu Studio projects with the materials and settings included, then reopened and sliced those to check they saved properly. the full set is about 749 g of PETG-CF and 115 g of TPU by the slicer estimate

updated the CAD, STEP, STLs and hardware list. the fastener and steel carts have shipping estimates, but the rod store isn't loading properly yet. still need that quote, a plan for cutting the steel and the last connector details. nothing printed or ordered
